Setting: Passwordless Capability Coverage At Least 90 Percent
Recommendation: Share of users who are passwordless-capable, from Microsoft's own isPasswordlessCapable field. Policy-aware, so unlike a raw registration count it only counts users whose registered passwordless method is actually allowed by the authentication methods policy. Read this as the destination metric: it will legitimately sit below target for most of a migration, and that is progress information rather than a failure, which is why it ships at Low severity. Two cautions when quoting it. First, passwordless is NOT the same as phishing-resistant. Microsoft's definition of this field covers FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business and Microsoft Authenticator passwordless phone sign-in, and that last one is push-based, so it is passwordless and still phishable. A tenant can raise this number by pushing phone sign-in without becoming meaningfully harder to attack. Second, the field's documented list omits certificate-based authentication, which Microsoft does count as phishing-resistant elsewhere, so a CBA-heavy tenant will score lower here than its actual posture warrants. For the phishing-resistant view specifically, use the Security Info user triage roster, which buckets on the registered methods themselves. Run the assessment with -Verbose to see where the two measures disagree and in which direction. Third: Microsoft Authenticator's per-target 'Authentication mode' setting (Any/Push/Passwordless in the admin center - see the Authentication Methods Policy Inventory's Settings column) gates whether a group's Authenticator registrations can count toward this field at all. A group locked to 'Push only' can have every user registered for Authenticator and still never be passwordless-capable through it, since push-only mode never offers the number-matching passwordless sign-in Microsoft's field actually measures - Graph's own isPasswordlessCapable calculation already accounts for this, so a low score alongside high Authenticator registration is worth checking against that setting specifically before assuming a registration-coverage problem.
